card.summary: The SAFE Act of 2026 amends the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978 and title 18 of the United States Code to reauthorize and reform surveillance authorities. It institutes new query procedures, reporting requirements, accountability standards for FBI violations, restrictions on reverse targeting, and limits on intelligence and law enforcement acquisition and purchase of personal data from data brokers.

summary: The SAFE Act of 2026 amends the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978 (FISA) and related laws to reauthorize certain surveillance authorities, impose tighter rules and querying restrictions on U.S. person data collected under Section 702, restrict the purchase of personal data from data brokers by intelligence and law enforcement agencies, expand transparency, and strengthen oversight mechanisms.

affected_groups.effect: Receive enhanced privacy protections regarding the querying, collection, and purchase of their communications and personal data by intelligence and law enforcement agencies.
Subject to stricter querying procedures, mandatory training, prior legal approvals, written justifications, and internal accountability or disciplinary tracking for compliance violations.
Must adhere to new limitations on acquiring or purchasing data from data brokers, establish compliance and accuracy procedures, and provide expanded reporting to Congress.
affected_groups.group: Intelligence Community and Law Enforcement Agencies

affected_groups.effect: Impacted by provisions governing directives, definitions of service providers, and consistent privacy demands across online and intermediary service providers.
affected_groups.group: Electronic Communication and Online Service Providers

key_provisions: Reauthorizes Title VII of FISA until April 20, 2028.
Restricts warrantless access by agencies to U.S. person communications returned in response to Section 702 queries, subject to specific exceptions.
Requires the FBI to implement training, prior approvals, written justifications, and affirmative elections for queries involving U.S. persons.

Prohibits intelligence agencies and law enforcement entities from acquiring or purchasing covered personal data and sensitive information from data brokers without a court order or applicable exception.
Expands the role and access of the amicus curiae in the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court (FISC), including the authority to seek review of legal questions.
Establishes criminal penalties for knowingly submitting false statements or material omissions to the FISA courts or unauthorized disclosures of applications.
Mandates periodic audits of FISA compliance by the Department of Justice Inspector General.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The SAFE Act of 2026 amends the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978 (FISA) and related laws to reauthorize certain surveillance authorities, impose tighter rules and querying restrictions on U.S. person data collected under Section 702, restrict the purchase of personal data from data brokers by intelligence and law enforcement agencies, expand transparency, and strengthen oversight mechanisms.
summary_detail.significance: The bill significantly alters federal intelligence gathering and law enforcement surveillance practices by placing statutory restrictions on warrantless database queries of U.S. persons, limiting the government's ability to purchase personal data from data brokers, and increasing judicial and congressional oversight.
